question.text: Rajendra is conducting DD on a real estate AIF. Which risk factor is UNIQUE to real estate AIFs compared to other AIF categories?

answer.text: Title risk, construction risk, and regulatory approval risk specific to real estate projects

explanation.text: The Logic: Real estate AIFs face industry-specific risks that are not typical of equity or debt AIFs: property title disputes, construction delays and cost overruns, and regulatory/approval risks (e.g., RERA registration, environmental clearances, change-of-land-use approvals). The Trap: Market risk, currency risk, and interest-rate risk affect many asset classes — they are not unique to real estate. Title and construction risks are specifically tied to real-estate projects. Note: The XIX-A workbook supports market risk, illiquidity/long-gestation risk, project risk, regulatory risk, and sector-specific risk disclosures in general terms; it does not separately enumerate "title risk," RERA, or environmental approvals as named real-estate-AIF risks. Treat the named risks here as general real-estate-investment knowledge.
